title: What can you say about pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for pantothenic acid (vitamin B5); the strongest is "Supports normal energy-yielding metabolism" (strong, 0.9-500 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Clears acne".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 0.4-500 mg a day. EU: at least 0.9 mg, 15% of the 6 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII).
supported_wordings.form: Calcium D-pantothenate or another salt on Health Canada's list, counted as pantothenic acid

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.
